role: Sr. Business Intelligence Engineer, B2C, Amazon Leo
responsibilities: Architect, build, and maintain foundational business datasets across our tech stack and other internal systems to support analytics, reporting, and customer growth use cases.
Develop SQL-based transformations, data models, and ETL/ELT workflows to structure and unify marketing and customer data for customer lifecycle use cases.
Design, optimize, and manage Amazon QuickSight dashboards that provide visibility into acquisition performance, attribution, and lifecycle funnels.
Conduct deep-dive analysis to identify funnel drop-offs, diagnose performance issues, uncover customer insights, and evaluate marketing effectiveness.
Translate ambiguous business questions into structured analytical approaches, data models, and scalable self-service tools.
Drive alignment on KPI definitions, measurement frameworks, taxonomy, and data governance across global marketing teams.
Collaborate closely with Product, Sales Ops, Data Science, and cross-functional partners to support experimentation, segmentation, forecasting, and predictive insights.

Communicate effectively with senior management audiences (e.g. narratives, inputs into weekly/monthly/quarterly business reviews).* Drive best practices in operational excellence, data modeling, and analysis. Ensure that BI solutions are correctly and efficiently supporting the business.* Participate in hiring activities and mentor junior team members

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: partnering with Data Engineering and Product teams to ensure complete, accurate, and actionable data across the full customer journey
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Accuracy, governance and operational-excellence language outweighs the two speed phrases ("fast, data-driven decisions", "agility of a startup").
evidence.domain_risk: build the analytics and data foundations that power Amazon Leo's global marketing engine
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Marketing and funnel analytics drive business decisions without regulatory or financial-reporting stakes, so it is moderate.
evidence.collaboration_width: Marketing; Product; Leadership; Data Engineering; Sales Ops; Data Science
evidence.data_team_maturity: You will own and evolve the backend data architecture within our Customer Dat (Treasure Data), building upon existing foundations as new data sources and use cases emerge.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: A B2C Analytics team exists with a CDP in place, but the business is new and the foundations are still being extended, so it is mid-stage.
evidence.jd_authorship: Design, optimize, and manage Amazon QuickSight dashboards that provide visibility into acquisition performance, attribution, and lifecycle funnels.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Bullets name the tools (QuickSight, Treasure Data CDP) and the specific analyses (attribution, lifecycle funnels), so the work is clear.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Design, optimize, and manage Amazon QuickSight dashboards that provide visibility into acquisition performance, attribution, and lifecycle funnels.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The primary audience is global marketing, per "acquisition performance, attribution, and lifecycle funnels".
evidence.autonomy_level: you will make independent strategic and technical decisions and drive your work forward with minimal oversight
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role defines measurement and owns the data architecture ("Architect, build, and maintain", "Drive alignment on KPI definitions").
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Machine learning appears only as background knowledge in the qualifications, not as AI tooling or AI-facing data work.
evidence.testing_framing: ensure complete, accurate, and actionable data across the full customer journey
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data accuracy is framed as something the candidate ensures, though without a named testing framework.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: You will be a strategic and technical owner ensuring that Amazon Leo Marketing can make accurate, timely, data-driven decisions.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Accuracy matters for marketing decisions but the role is framed around building measurement, so the risk register is moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: building upon existing foundations as new data sources and use cases emerge
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: New datasets and measurement frameworks are built on an existing CDP foundation.
evidence.loss_aversion: ensuring that Amazon Leo Marketing can make accurate, timely, data-driven decisions — accuracy is a goal, not the role's main framing.
